units.text: The weather ETL job dies with a MemoryError on the 12 GB parquet dump. It's a pandas script, etl/weather_daily.py. Should I just rent a bigger box?

A bigger box works but hides the problem. The general trade-off: pandas is eager and single-threaded, it materialises the whole frame in memory, and a 12 GB parquet file easily becomes 40 GB of pandas objects once strings are decoded. Polars is lazy by default, multi-threaded, and its streaming engine processes a query in batches, so memory stays roughly constant regardless of input size. DuckDB is a third option with similar properties and SQL as the interface. Both of the latter read parquet natively.
Let's rewrite it in polars then, I've wanted an excuse. Keep the output identical, the downstream dashboards read daily_weather.parquet.

Rewrote etl/weather_daily.py with `pl.scan_parquet` and the same group-by. First run still blew up: `sink_parquet` ran the whole plan in memory. The fix was `collect(engine='streaming')` combined with `sink_parquet`; in polars 1.x the streaming engine is opt-in per query, and without it the lazy frame is still materialised at the end. With streaming on, peak memory is 2.1 GB for the 12 GB input.

Output check: the new daily_weather.parquet has the same 3,652 rows and the same column set as the pandas version; I compared both with a frame-equality assertion including dtypes. One difference I had to handle: polars writes dates as Date, pandas wrote datetime64[ns]; I cast to Datetime to keep the downstream readers unchanged.
Kick off the full job now and tell me when it's done, I'm going for lunch.
Started; it is at 30% after two minutes, so about seven more minutes to go. I will report when it finishes.

expected.content: The weather ETL job (etl/weather_daily.py) was rewritten from pandas to polars in April 2026 because the pandas version hit MemoryError on a 12 GB parquet input.
In polars 1.x, sink_parquet on a lazy frame still materialises in memory unless the streaming engine is enabled with collect(engine='streaming'); with it, the 12 GB job peaks at about 2.1 GB.
Downstream dashboards read daily_weather.parquet, so its schema must stay identical; the date column is cast to Datetime to match the old pandas datetime64 output.
